subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a corporate riot-control interceptor vehicle, styled like a Cyberpunk 2077 armored van with a roof water cannon, neon light bars, and corp logos in yellow/cyan/magenta against dark armored panels. I'll keep the build API usage limited to well-known calls like createBuilder, joint, and part methods to stay correct.

Now I'm sketching out the vehicle's dimensions—roughly 5.6m long, 2.2m wide, 2.5m tall—plus wheel placement and the joint skeleton for the chassis, wheels, steering, and turret, deciding to favor safer box-based geometry over riskier loft sections to avoid API uncertainty.

I'm working out a side-profile extrusion for the hull: a polygon outline in the z-y plane, extruded along the x-axis to give it width, forming a wedge-shaped body with the cabin as a separate piece layered on top. Defining hull profile points...

I need to position the wheels outside the body silhouette rather than overlapping it, so I'll narrow the body width and offset the wheel centers wider with small fender flare boxes on top for detail. Wheel hubs sit at ground level with radius 0.45, keeping things simple.

For the windscreen, I'm figuring out the tilted glass plane that matches the cab's sloped roofline, calculating rotation about the X-axis so the thin glass box aligns with the slope direction in the yz-plane.

Next I'm adding small slit windows with cage bars on the cab sides.

For the rear, I'll add double doors with a decal and a magenta neon tail light strip. On the roof, I'm placing a water cannon turret with yaw and pitch joints, a barrel with a flared nozzle and glowing cyan tip, plus a pair of pressure tank cylinders with cyan gauge lighting behind it. I'll also add roof light bars split magenta and cyan at the front.

For the body, I'm adding grille neon strips, cyan underglow on the rockers, a bull bar with yellow hazard stripes, glowing headlight slits, a push bar with stripe texture up front, and a side decal for an invented corp logo like "MERIDIAN CIVIC DEFENSE" with a hex emblem rendered on a plane facing outward on the side of the vehicle.

I'm working out which direction the text should face on each side so it reads correctly to an outside viewer, given the plane's orientation and up vector, then adding "RIOT SUPPRESSION UNIT" text plus a unit number as additional svg textures alongside the hazard stripes.

Now I'm sketching the remaining textures: a glowing cyan "STAND DOWN" LED sign and an amber "DISPERSE" banner on the cab roof, plus rear door graphics, headlights, and a number plate, giving roughly five texture layers total for that cyberpunk riot-vehicle look. For the body paint, I'm defining a custom dark navy-graphite material with a lighter highlight toward the top panels.

Now I'm defining the wheels with tires, glowing rim rings, and spokes, setting up the wheel joints parented to the chassis with hub positions and steering joint stubs for the front wheels.

Adding rear door hinge joints with panel geometry, then setting up the turret with yaw and pitch joints for rotation.

Still working out geometry...

Now I'm designing the twin water tanks mounted on the rear roof—horizontal cylinders colored matte white with cyan "H2O" decal planes and a glowing water-level glass tube on the rear end for that corporate utility-bot look.

I'm also placing a roof-mounted light bar near the windscreen edge, split into magenta and cyan segmented glowing panels, with a separate LED sign plane stacked above it for displaying text.

Now I'm building out the front end: a hood region leading to a ram-bumper assembly with hazard texture and push-bar tubes, slim glowing headlight boxes flanking a dark grille, and a cyan neon strip running along the lower front edge.

Adding side armor skirts with yellow stripe accents, plus magenta neon trim along the beltline and a logo decal on the flank for extra detailing.

For the cab windows, I'm positioning sloped side glass panels near the windscreen with three vertical security bars across each one, and I'm thinking about adding vent details on the rear cargo sides instead of extra window ports, before moving on to antenna placement.

For the rear end, I'm adding a magenta taillight bar, split door lines, license plate, bumper step, and a hex-emblem decal with stripes for the rear door graphic, plus mirror stalks with small magenta glow boxes. For rigging, I'm setting the chassis as the spine role and wheels as hinge joints, then working out wheel cylinder geometry so the lowest point touches the ground at y=0.

Now I'm sketching out helper functions for box and cylinder geometry, plus a `P` part helper and `G` glow helper that attach meshes to the chassis bone with position and color options. I'm also starting to design the side logo texture as an SVG with a hex emblem and "MERIDIAN" branding text in yellow and white.

Writing SVG code...

I'm also planning additional decals: a rear hex graphic with "RSU-9" and a barcode, a tank label styled as "AQUA-JET" with a blue drop icon, and an invented plate reading "MCD-2077", skipping the windscreen HUD but keeping glowing sensor eyes on the front. Each texture gets mapped onto a plane geometry, with a helper function for placing and orienting these decal planes on bones.

Working out the orientation math now for each decal — figuring out which local axis faces which direction so text reads correctly from the viewer's perspective, checking the rear doors, the side panels, and confirming the up/right vectors align properly for readability.

Checking the body extrusion for the cab front: setting up the outline points in the z-y plane, extruding along x with a thickness of 1.9 and a small bevel, and making sure the axis orientation keeps things centered.

Skipping roof hazard details, but adding a few horizontal armor ribs along the flanks, plus thin dark door seam boxes on the cab for detail.

Still building door outlines...

Adding front grille slats, a mirror, wiper rods, and a ram-style front frame using rod shapes.

For the interior I'll keep it hidden behind dark-tinted glass rather than modeling seats, and I'm checking clearances for the roof turret, tank placement, and barrel pitch so nothing collides with the windshield or light bar.

Still adjusting the turret geometry so the barrel clears the sign and light bar, repositioning the pivot height, and now defining the yaw drum, trunnion cheeks, and pitch joint coordinates for the barrel rod.

I'm working out the barrel rod and nozzle placement along the z-axis, then positioning the fuel tanks behind the turret base so they don't collide with the drum, before routing a curved hose from the tank to the turret mount.

Now I'm sketching a thin cyan glow strip along the barrel top, and starting the wheel construction function with a tire cylinder in dark flat material.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Still designing fender flares...

For colors I'm thinking a cyberpunk palette: dark graphite body with yellow 2077-style accents and cyan highlights.

I'm sketching underbody skid plates, axle rods, rear bumper and taillights, plus mirror arms mounted at the front pillars, keeping total part count manageable around 200 for a ~400 line script. Now I'm working out door line details using symmetric side offsets with dark trim boxes marking the panel seams.

I'm now checking where the cab roof slope intersects the door and window heights, placing a trapezoid window box positioned to fit under the sloped roofline without clipping, then starting the door line geometry at the front of the cab.

Writing door and handle geometry...

Adding more lighting details...

I'm placing the taillight glow strip and working out the rear door geometry—width, height, hinge pivots, and door box placement with a logo graphic on each.

Still writing part definitions...
